From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Threshold points

- **The disclosure is stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. We should require an updated disclosure, with the warranties repeated at signing and at Completion. We should also say expressly that later disclosures do not qualify signing warranties unless we agree.
- **The Disclosure Letter undercuts the Seller's covering note.** The Letter itself confirms that there is no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay assignment, and no confirmed scope for the data incident. The note's descriptions ("addressed", "not expected to be material", "ordinary-course", "settled") are advocacy, not facts. None should appear in the SPA.
- **Several known risks call for specific indemnities.** These are Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay, the export incident and Sandbar. Because we know about them, warranties alone will not protect us, particularly under the Seller's knowledge and disclosure positions.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** General warranty claims are capped at 20% of the price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer should want:** A higher cap, for example 40–50% of the price (AUD 9.6m–12m). If W&I insurance is used, the cap should be structured around the policy limit plus a Seller retention. The cap should apply to general warranty claims only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%. Counter at 50%, and be prepared to land at about 30–35% if the specific indemnities and fundamental regime below are secured. **Reason:** 20% is low given that about 30% of revenue (Bluefen), IP ownership (Ironquay) and a live privacy incident are all exposed.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim. AUD 250,000 basket operating as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - De minimis of about AUD 10,000–15,000, with related claims aggregated for de minimis purposes.
  - A tipping basket of about AUD 120,000–180,000 (roughly 0.5–0.75%), so that once it is exceeded we recover from the first dollar.
  - Neither threshold to apply to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, covenant or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible. Insist on a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims. **Reason:** A deductible combined with a high per-claim floor removes a meaningful slice of genuine loss, and lets related small claims (for example, individual data-subject claims) escape entirely.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** 18 months after Completion. The Seller adds that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties, so that at least two full audit cycles are covered. Separate and longer periods should apply to the other categories (see SPA-N-004, 014 and 016).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months, and accept no less than 2 audit cycles. Reject the "all Claims" extension. **Reason:** 18 months may capture only one audit, and the extension would silently shorten the time limits for tax, title and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties would carry the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title, shares and capital, no encumbrances, solvency) capped at 100% of the price.
  - No de minimis or basket on those warranties.
  - A time limit of at least 6 years, consistent with the NSW contract limitation period, or longer if the SPA is executed as a deed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. **Reason:** If we do not get the shares we bargained for, we lose the whole AUD 24m, so a 20% cap with 18 months is commercially incoherent. "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An express carve-out so that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause applies to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers.
  - Non-reliance should not be framed to defeat statutory misleading or deceptive conduct claims (ACL s 18) where these arise from fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Treat this as non-negotiable. **Reason:** Exclusions of liability for one's own fraud are generally unenforceable anyway, but "all Claims of any nature" invites argument and should be fixed expressly.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Only specific disclosures count. Each must be made against a specific warranty, with enough detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  - Data room contents are not deemed disclosed, or at most are deemed disclosed only where a matter is fairly and specifically apparent from an identified document.
  - Public records are limited to named searches (ASIC and PPSR) obtained on a specified date.
  - An agreed USB or archive copy of the data room is held by both sides.
  - Fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims cannot be qualified by any disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Accept only the specific-disclosure standard. **Reason:** General disclosure turns the warranties into a "find it yourself" exercise and would neutralise protection on the exact issues the Letter already flags.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Preferably, an express provision that the Buyer's knowledge does not reduce claims (pro-sandbagging).
  - As a fallback, the bar is limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
  - No constructive or imputed knowledge, and no knowledge attributed from advisers.
  - The bar never applies to specific indemnities, tax, fundamental warranties or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "discoverable" and "advisers". Push for pro-sandbagging and fall back to actual knowledge of named individuals. **Reason:** As drafted, our own diligence would extinguish our claims, which penalises thoroughness.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (about AUD 3.6m, around 30% of FY26 revenue)
- **Seller position:** The consent is "addressed". The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms that no final consent has been provided and no evidence exists that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A condition precedent requiring unconditional written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, not withdrawn at Completion.
  - All cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, or imposing no obligations or cost on the Buyer or the Company that are unacceptable to the Buyer.
  - The condition waivable by the Buyer only.
  - Seller obligation of "all reasonable endeavours", with Buyer consultation on all approaches to Bluefen.
  - A sunset date and termination right. Consider a price adjustment or earn-out mechanism if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates within, for example, 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Strengthen the condition precedent. Do not accept "delivery of a letter" as satisfaction. **Reason:** A consent that is conditional, or whose conditions are unmet, could still allow Bluefen to terminate, which puts about 30% of revenue at risk.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m)
- **Seller position:** A release will be provided after Completion. The Letter confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge has been given. DD-003 contains a change-control clause (cl 8.1) and a discharge clause (cl 9.2).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The full amount treated as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics and paid directly to Riverlark from the purchase price at Completion.
  - Before Completion, a payout letter confirming the exact amount, including break costs and per-diem interest.
  - At Completion, a deed of release and discharge of all security over the Company and the shares, together with PPSR financing statement releases or an undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amounts.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. **Reason:** The change of control may trigger default under cl 8.1, and paying the price without a discharge in hand leaves security over the business we have just bought.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)
- **Seller position:** A "matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The Letter is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses plus all associated costs treated as Debt or transaction costs, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller. Associated costs include employer superannuation (SG is currently 12%; confirm whether the bonuses are ordinary time earnings), NSW payroll tax (confirm the current rate and thresholds), workers' compensation and other on-costs.
  - The bonuses either paid through Company payroll at Completion with PAYG withholding, funded via the funds flow, or ringfenced in a retention.
  - A specific indemnity for any unpaid or under-calculated amounts.
  - Clarity on what happens if the continued-employment conditions fail after Completion, so that any obligation crystallising later does not fall on the Company.
- **Recommendation:** Require the bonuses to appear in the funds flow as a price deduction. **Reason:** The liability sits with the Company, which we are buying. "Matter for the Seller" has no legal effect unless the SPA makes the Seller bear it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (DD-004 / DD-010)
- **Seller position:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate". The Letter confirms AUD 180,000 is open, there is no bank verification and no confirmatory assignment exists.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - As a condition precedent or Completion deliverable: evidence that every SOW3 fee has been paid in cleared funds, plus a signed confirmatory IP assignment deed from Ironquay (with moral rights consents as relevant) covering all SOW3 Project Materials.
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering all Loss from the Company not owning, or being unable to use, the SOW3 materials. This includes third-party claims, re-development or licensing costs, and business interruption.
  - The indemnity should be dollar-one, outside the general cap, with at least 6 years' survival, and backed by a retention or escrow (for example, AUD 500k–1m, to be sized on how important SOW3 is to the product).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the payment-only scope and make the assignment a Completion deliverable. **Reason:** The risk is that the Company does not own its own IP, not merely an AUD 180k debt.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." The Letter states that access, scope and the need to notify are all undetermined (about 1,240 records). That position dates from 22 September.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A full updated disclosure now, including any forensic report, access logs, link-expiry and recipient evidence, the Notifiable Data Breaches (Privacy Act) assessment and its conclusion, and any OAIC or individual notifications. The assessment is required to be completed within 30 days, so its status by now is itself a diligence point.
  - Completion of the assessment and remediation before Completion.
  - A specific indemnity, dollar-one, outside the cap and thresholds, with an extended survival period, covering investigation, notification, remediation, third-party and representative claims, and regulatory costs. Civil penalties may not be lawfully indemnifiable, so the drafting should cover them to the maximum extent permitted by law.
  - A retention and appropriate privacy warranties.
  - No reference to "not material" anywhere in the SPA.
- **Recommendation:** Require specific indemnity, retention and updated disclosure. **Reason:** The facts are unresolved and the 30-day assessment clock has likely run, so the Seller's materiality assessment carries no weight.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011, 3 × AUD 110,000)
- **Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs. The Letter says the three renewals should be read together and does not say whether they are avoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Disclosure of the dates, terms, termination rights, and who approved each renewal and when.
  - Related contracts aggregated for material-contract and conduct-of-business thresholds.
  - Confirmation whether the split brought each renewal under an approval threshold.
  - If the renewals were not in the ordinary course, or were entered after the relevant date, the Seller bears the cost through a price adjustment, Debt treatment or a specific indemnity, or arranges termination.
  - Pre-Completion conduct covenants requiring Buyer consent for any related contracts exceeding the threshold in aggregate.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Require aggregation and investigate. **Reason:** Three identical related renewals that must be read together suggest contract splitting, and AUD 330k is significant value leaving the Company.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13), and limitation and reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:** The reverse default. The general cap, thresholds, time limit and knowledge or disclosure qualifiers should apply only to general warranty claims. Separate tailored regimes should apply to:
  - fundamental warranties
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity
  - each specific indemnity
  - covenant and undertaking breaches
  - fraud (no limits)

  The SPA should also include an express no-double-recovery clause, but no cross-category erosion of caps.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Redraft the limitations schedule by category. **Reason:** The "unless expressly stated" default means any drafting gap collapses our negotiated indemnities into the 20% / 18-month regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. The Letter expressly notes that the Buyer has not verified this.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent verification through current ASIC company extracts and historical share issue and transfer records reconciled to the register.
  - The constitution and any shareholders' agreement checked for pre-emption rights.
  - Confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, ESOP or phantom equity (cross-check against the DD-005 bonuses).
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, including any security over the shares (Riverlark).
  - Title and no-encumbrance warranties at fundamental level.
  - Completion deliverables: executed transfers, share certificates or lost-certificate indemnities, register updates, and releases.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on DD-012 alone. Complete our own verification before signing. **Reason:** A register is evidence, not proof, and the title warranty is only worth its fundamental-level protection.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller position:** "Settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A separate tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including the payroll tax and super associated with the bonuses, with:
    - no de minimis or basket
    - a cap at 100% of the price
    - a time limit running to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer (for example, 60 days after it expires, or a flat 5–7 years)
    - conduct-of-claims and tax-return provisions.
  - **IP:** Robust ownership, non-infringement and sufficiency warranties with an extended time limit, for example 3–4 years. The Ironquay indemnity should sit separately (SPA-N-011).
- **Recommendation:** Record as open, not settled. **Reason:** Under the Seller's general regime, the 18-month limit would expire well before the ATO could amend, and IP is the core value of an analytics business.

---

## Priority summary

| Priority | Issues |
|---|---|
| **Walk-away / non-negotiable** | 005 Fraud, 004 Fundamental, 009 Riverlark discharge at Completion, 014 Category separation |
| **Must-have before signing** | 008 Bluefen CP, 011 Ironquay assignment, 012 Incident update and indemnity, 010 Bonuses in funds flow, 015 Title verification, 016 Tax indemnity |
| **Core negotiation** | 001 Cap, 002 Thresholds, 003 Time limit, 006 Disclosure, 007 Knowledge |
| **Investigate and price** | 013 Sandbar |

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Request an updated Disclosure Letter and incident file.
2. Order ASIC and PPSR searches.
3. Request the Riverlark payout letter and Bluefen correspondence.
4. Prepare a mark-up that restructures cl 12 by category.
5. Consider whether W&I insurance would change the cap and threshold strategy.

NSW counsel should confirm the limitation periods, the payroll tax and super calculations, and the enforceability points before the mark-up is issued.

- **Seller position:** The consent is "addressed". The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms that no final consent has been provided and no evidence exists that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A condition precedent requiring unconditional written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, not withdrawn at Completion.
  - All cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, or imposing no obligations or cost on the Buyer or the Company that are unacceptable to the Buyer.
  - The condition waivable by the Buyer only.
  - Seller obligation of "all reasonable endeavours", with Buyer consultation on all approaches to Bluefen.
  - A sunset date and termination right. Consider a price adjustment or earn-out mechanism if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates within, for example, 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Strengthen the condition precedent. Do not accept "delivery of a letter" as satisfaction. **Reason:** A consent that is conditional, or whose conditions are unmet, could still allow Bluefen to terminate, which puts about 30% of revenue at risk.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m)
- **Seller position:** A release will be provided after Completion. The Letter confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge has been given. DD-003 contains a change-control clause (cl 8.1) and a discharge clause (cl 9.2).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The full amount treated as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics and paid directly to Riverlark from the purchase price at Completion.
  - Before Completion, a payout letter confirming the exact amount, including break costs and per-diem interest.
  - At Completion, a deed of release and discharge of all security over the Company and the shares, together with PPSR financing statement releases or an undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days.
  - A specific indemnity for any residual amounts.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. **Reason:** The change of control may trigger default under cl 8.1, and paying the price without a discharge in hand leaves security over the business we have just bought.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)
- **Seller position:** A "matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The Letter is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses plus all associated costs treated as Debt or transaction costs, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller. Associated costs include employer superannuation (SG is currently 12%; confirm whether the bonuses are ordinary time earnings), NSW payroll tax (confirm the current rate and thresholds), workers' compensation and other on-costs.
  - The bonuses either paid through Company payroll at Completion with PAYG withholding, funded via the funds flow, or ringfenced in a retention.
  - A specific indemnity for any unpaid or under-calculated amounts.
  - Clarity on what happens if the continued-employment conditions fail after Completion, so that any obligation crystallising later does not fall on the Company.
- **Recommendation:** Require the bonuses to appear in the funds flow as a price deduction. **Reason:** The liability sits with the Company, which we are buying. "Matter for the Seller" has no legal effect unless the SPA makes the Seller bear it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (DD-004 / DD-010)
- **Seller position:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate". The Letter confirms AUD 180,000 is open, there is no bank verification and no confirmatory assignment exists.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - As a condition precedent or Completion deliverable: evidence that every SOW3 fee has been paid in cleared funds, plus a signed confirmatory IP assignment deed from Ironquay (with moral rights consents as relevant) covering all SOW3 Project Materials.
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering all Loss from the Company not owning, or being unable to use, the SOW3 materials. This includes third-party claims, re-development or licensing costs, and business interruption.
  - The indemnity should be dollar-one, outside the general cap, with at least 6 years' survival, and backed by a retention or escrow (for example, AUD 500k–1m, to be sized on how important SOW3 is to the product).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the payment-only scope and make the assignment a Completion deliverable. **Reason:** The risk is that the Company does not own its own IP, not merely an AUD 180k debt.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." The Letter states that access, scope and the need to notify are all undetermined (about 1,240 records). That position dates from 22 September.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A full updated disclosure now, including any forensic report, access logs, link-expiry and recipient evidence, the Notifiable Data Breaches (Privacy Act) assessment and its conclusion, and any OAIC or individual notifications. The assessment is required to be completed within 30 days, so its status by now is itself a diligence point.
  - Completion of the assessment and remediation before Completion.
  - A specific indemnity, dollar-one, outside the cap and thresholds, with an extended survival period, covering investigation, notification, remediation, third-party and representative claims, and regulatory costs. Civil penalties may not be lawfully indemnifiable, so the drafting should cover them to the maximum extent permitted by law.
  - A retention and appropriate privacy warranties.
  - No reference to "not material" anywhere in the SPA.
- **Recommendation:** Require specific indemnity, retention and updated disclosure. **Reason:** The facts are unresolved and the 30-day assessment clock has likely run, so the Seller's materiality assessment carries no weight.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011, 3 × AUD 110,000)
- **Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs. The Letter says the three renewals should be read together and does not say whether they are avoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Disclosure of the dates, terms, termination rights, and who approved each renewal and when.
  - Related contracts aggregated for material-contract and conduct-of-business thresholds.
  - Confirmation whether the split brought each renewal under an approval threshold.
  - If the renewals were not in the ordinary course, or were entered after the relevant date, the Seller bears the cost through a price adjustment, Debt treatment or a specific indemnity, or arranges termination.
  - Pre-Completion conduct covenants requiring Buyer consent for any related contracts exceeding the threshold in aggregate.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Require aggregation and investigate. **Reason:** Three identical related renewals that must be read together suggest contract splitting, and AUD 330k is significant value leaving the Company.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13), and limitation and reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:** The reverse default. The general cap, thresholds, time limit and knowledge or disclosure qualifiers should apply only to general warranty claims. Separate tailored regimes should apply to:
  - fundamental warranties
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity
  - each specific indemnity
  - covenant and undertaking breaches
  - fraud (no limits)

  The SPA should also include an express no-double-recovery clause, but no cross-category erosion of caps.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Redraft the limitations schedule by category. **Reason:** The "unless expressly stated" default means any drafting gap collapses our negotiated indemnities into the 20% / 18-month regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced" by the share register at DD-012. The Letter expressly notes that the Buyer has not verified this.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Independent verification through current ASIC company extracts and historical share issue and transfer records reconciled to the register.
  - The constitution and any shareholders' agreement checked for pre-emption rights.
  - Confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, ESOP or phantom equity (cross-check against the DD-005 bonuses).
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, including any security over the shares (Riverlark).
  - Title and no-encumbrance warranties at fundamental level.
  - Completion deliverables: executed transfers, share certificates or lost-certificate indemnities, register updates, and releases.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on DD-012 alone. Complete our own verification before signing. **Reason:** A register is evidence, not proof, and the title warranty is only worth its fundamental-level protection.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller position:** "Settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A separate tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including the payroll tax and super associated with the bonuses, with:
    - no de minimis or basket
    - a cap at 100% of the price
    - a time limit running to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer (for example, 60 days after it expires, or a flat 5–7 years)
    - conduct-of-claims and tax-return provisions.
  - **IP:** Robust ownership, non-infringement and sufficiency warranties with an extended time limit, for example 3–4 years. The Ironquay indemnity should sit separately (SPA-N-011).
- **Recommendation:** Record as open, not settled. **Reason:** Under the Seller's general regime, the 18-month limit would expire well before the ATO could amend, and IP is the core value of an analytics business.
